facts.statement: The species Santanaraptor placidus was first described by Kellner in 1999.
facts.quote: The type species is S. placidus, first described by Kellner in 1999.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was unearthed in 1996 from the Romualdo Formation in Ceará State, northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: It was unearthed in 1996 from the Romualdo Formation (Santana Group) in the Ceará State, northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: Santanaraptor lived in South America during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: Santanaraptor (meaning "Santana Formation thief") is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Early Cretaceous (late Aptian-early Albian), about 112 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype is a juvenile partial skeleton containing three caudal vertebrae, pelvic and hindlimb bones, and preserved soft tissue.
facts.quote: The holotype (MN 4802-V) is a juvenile partial skeleton consisting of three caudal vertebrae with chevrons, ischia, femora, tibia, fibula, pes, and soft tissue.

facts.statement: Skin impressions under the left foot show preserved scales.
facts.quote: Skin impressions under the left foot are also preserved, showing scales.

facts.statement: It is presumed to have had long arms, three-fingered hands, and slim hindlimbs, similar to Dilong and Guanlong.
facts.quote: It is presumed to be similar to Dilong and Guanlong in that it had long arms, three fingered hands, and slim hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Santanaraptor is now classified as a basal coelurosaur based on features found on the femur, rather than a maniraptoran theropod.
facts.quote: Santanaraptor was originally thought to be a maniraptoran theropod when it was first discovered. However, it is now thought to be a basal coelurosaur based on several features present on the femur.

facts.statement: The classification of Santanaraptor as a tyrannosauroid is debated because its supposed tyrannosauroid traits are widespread in Coelurosauria and its foot resembles noasaurids.
facts.quote: However, this position has been criticised, as the supposed tyrannosauroid characters are widely distributed in Coelurosauria, and several aspects of the foot are more similar to noasaurids.

facts.statement: A 2025 study suggests Santanaraptor could be either a megaraptoran within Tyrannosauroidea or an early branching maniraptoromorph outside that group, depending on the phylogenetic method used.
facts.quote: In their comprehensive revision of Santanaraptor and Mirischia, Delcourt et al. (2025) recovered the former in two different positions: as a megaraptoran within Tyrannosauroidea based on equal weight phylogenetic analyses and as an early branching maniraptoromorph based on implied weight phylogenetic analyses, forming a clade with Tanycolagreus, Mirischia and Juratyrant outside Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Santanaraptor placidus lived in South America during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 108 million years ago.
facts.quote: Santanaraptor placidus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Santanaraptor («rapaz de la Formación Santana») es un género de dinosaurio terópodo celurosauriano, que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 108 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Santana Formation across Pernambuco, Piauí, and Ceará states in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Santana de Pernambuco, Piauí y Ceará cerca de poblado de Santana do camiri al noreste de Brasil.

facts.statement: Santanaraptor was a small carnivore about 1.25 meters long, known from a juvenile holotype containing tail vertebrae, pelvic and leg bones, and soft tissue.
facts.quote: Fue un pequeño carnívoro de alrededor del 1,25 metros de largo y se basa en el holotipo MN 4802-V, un ejemplar juvenil, que consiste en tres vértebras 3 caudales con cheurón, isquion, fémur, tibia, fíbula, pie, y tejido suave.

facts.statement: Fossilized soft tissues include epidermis, muscle fibers, and possibly blood vessels.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de tejido blando epidermis, fibras de músculos y posiblemente vasos sanguíneos.

facts.statement: The type species S. placidus was first described by Kellner in 1999.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es S. placidus, descrita por primera vez por Kellner en 1999.

facts.statement: The species was originally considered a maniraptor when first described.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es S. placidus, descrita por primera vez por Kellner en 1999. y originalmente considerada un maniraptor.

facts.statement: Today, Santanaraptor is considered a basal Coelurosauria due to specific features found on the femur.
facts.quote: Sin embargo hoy se lo considera un Coelurosauria basal debido a varias particularidades encontradas en el fémur.

facts.statement: Santanaraptor is thought to be closely related to the Early Jurassic coelurosaur Ornitholestes based on similarities in the ischium.
facts.quote: Santanaraptor debió haber estado cercanamente relacionado con Ornitholestes, un celurosauriano temprano del Jurásico superior, basados en similitudes del isquion, hueso de la pelvis.

facts.statement: The time range for Santanaraptor is estimated between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
